text: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron while they were still in Egypt, saying,
This month is to be the first month for you — the beginning of your calendar year.
Tell the whole community of Israel that on the tenth day of this month each family is to take a lamb, one per household.
If a household is too small to eat a whole lamb, they should share one with the nearest neighboring family, splitting it according to how many people and how much each can eat.
The animal must be a healthy, flawless year-old male, taken from either the sheep or the goats.
Keep it watched until the fourteenth day of the month, when the whole assembly of Israel will slaughter their animals at twilight.
Then take some of its blood and apply it to the two doorposts and the beam above the door of the house where the meal will be eaten.
That same night, eat the meat roasted over fire, along with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
Do not eat it raw or boiled — only roasted whole over the fire, including the head, legs, and internal organs.
Leave nothing until morning; whatever remains by daybreak must be burned up completely.
Eat it this way: belt tied, sandals on your feet, walking stick in hand, eating quickly. This is the LORD's Passover.
That night I will pass through Egypt and strike down every firstborn, of people and animals alike, and bring judgment on all the gods of Egypt — I am the LORD.
The blood will mark the houses where you are staying; when I see it, I will pass over you, and no destructive plague will touch you when I strike Egypt.
You are to remember this day always, celebrating it as a festival to the LORD in every generation, a lasting rule.
For seven days eat only unleavened bread. Remove all yeast from your homes on the first day — anyone who eats something leavened during that week is to be cut off from Israel.
On the first day hold a sacred gathering, and again on the seventh day. No regular work is allowed on those days, except preparing food that everyone needs to eat.
Keep the Festival of Unleavened Bread, because on this very day I brought your people out of Egypt — observe it forever, generation after generation.
Starting the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month, eat unleavened bread through the evening of the twenty-first day.
For those seven days no yeast should be found anywhere in your homes — anyone who eats anything leavened, whether a foreigner or native-born, is to be cut off from the community.
Eat nothing containing yeast; wherever you live, eat unleavened bread.
Moses called together all the elders of Israel and told them, Go pick out lambs for your families and slaughter the Passover animal.
Take a bunch of hyssop, dip it in the blood collected in a basin, and wipe it on the doorframe's beam and both posts. None of you should leave your house until morning.
For the LORD will move through the land to strike Egypt, and seeing the blood on the doorframe, he will pass over that entrance and not let the destroyer come in to strike you.
Keep this practice as a permanent rule for you and your descendants.
When you reach the land the LORD is giving you as promised, continue observing this ceremony.
And when your children ask you what this ritual means to you,

tell them it is the sacrifice of the LORD's Passover, because he passed over the homes of the Israelites in Egypt when he struck down the Egyptians but spared our households. At that, the people bowed low and worshiped.
So the Israelites went and did exactly as the LORD had directed Moses and Aaron.
At midnight the LORD struck down every firstborn in Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh on his throne to the firstborn of the prisoner locked in the dungeon, and all the firstborn livestock too.
Pharaoh got up in the night, along with all his officials and the rest of Egypt, and a loud wail rose across the land, because there was no house without someone dead in it.
That night Pharaoh sent for Moses and Aaron and said, Get up and leave my people, you and the Israelites — go and worship the LORD as you requested.
Take your flocks and herds too, just as you said, and go — and ask a blessing for me as well.
The Egyptians pressed the people to hurry out of the land, saying, Otherwise we will all be dead.
So the people carried off their bread dough before it had risen, wrapping the kneading bowls in cloth and carrying them on their shoulders.
The Israelites had also done what Moses instructed, asking the Egyptians for silver, gold jewelry, and clothing.
The LORD made the Egyptians favorably disposed toward the people, so they gave them what they asked for — the Israelites came away with the wealth of Egypt.
The Israelites set out from Rameses toward Succoth — about six hundred thousand men on foot, not counting women and children.
A large crowd of non-Israelites went with them too, along with huge numbers of sheep, goats, and cattle.
They baked flat, unleavened loaves from the dough they had brought from Egypt, since it hadn't risen — they had been rushed out of Egypt with no time to prepare food for the road.
The Israelites had lived in Egypt for four hundred thirty years.
At the end of exactly four hundred thirty years, on that very day, all the LORD's people marched out of Egypt.
This is a night to be kept watch over in honor of the LORD, since he brought them out of Egypt that night — a night all Israelites are to keep watch over for the LORD, generation after generation.
The LORD told Moses and Aaron: These are the rules for the Passover meal — no outsider may eat it.
But any slave a man has purchased may eat it, once he has been circumcised.
A temporary resident or hired worker may not eat it.
It must be eaten inside one house — don't carry any of the meat outside, and don't break any of its bones.
The entire community of Israel is to observe it.

If a foreigner living among you wants to keep the Passover for the LORD, every male in his household must be circumcised first; then he may take part, treated the same as someone born in the land — but no uncircumcised person may eat it.
The same law applies equally to the native-born and to the foreigner living among you.
All the Israelites did just as the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron.
And on that very day the LORD brought the Israelites out of Egypt, group by group.
